title: Active ordering and reflex testing of the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index within the primary care preventive health examination ('Check-Up')
summary:
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) represents a highly prevalent condition in Germany. However, it is crucial to emphasize that only a minority of patients with MASLD develop liver fibrosis requiring treatment; thus, adequate screening must be performed to correctly identify patients in need of therapy. Guidelines recommend this screening as a two-step procedure, utilizing the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index as the initial step. In cases of an elevated FIB-4 score, the result should be confirmed using specialized ultrasound modalities before a MASLD-specific therapy is indicated, if applicable. These specialized ultrasound-based examinations are performed in a specialist care setting following referral.
The FIB-4 index is a laboratory-based tool. Although its parameters can be determined easily and cost-effectively, it is assumed that the test is often unknown and underutilized in primary care.

Objective: The objective  is to investigate how frequently a FIB-4 test is actively requested in the primary care setting during routine health examinations, and how often the index can be determined via laboratory-level reflex testing based on additional blood values ordered during the "Check-Up".
Furthermore, a second laboratory-based tool, the so-called Liver Risk Score, will be evaluated as an alternative to the FIB-4 index.
conditions: Fatty (change of) liver, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of a laboratory database in the time period 01/2025 - 12/2025

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participation in preventive health care examination "Check-Up"
Exclusion criteria:
